source.title: Robustly Improving LLM Fairness in Realistic Settings via Interpretability

record.tranche_reason: Uses SAE attribution and logit-lens analysis as exploratory tools for investigating bias prediction, but does not test superposition, polysemanticity, feature recovery, or feature dimensionality.
record.gate_note: The fairness evaluations and affine concept editing do not measure superposition or its geometry. The exploratory white-box analysis reports SAE/logit-lens findings about demographic-related features; these do not establish the claim versions about recoverability, feature overlap, or dimensionality, so they are recorded as related findings under fits_no_version.
record.test_reason: A hiring-bias study. It uses linear demographic directions (difference of means, affine concept editing) and, in an exploratory appendix, SAE attribution patching as tools. It reports bias rates and mitigation performance. It never measures superposition, polysemanticity, SAE feature recovery or completeness, or feature dimensionality. The SAE analysis only reports a qualitative correlation of demographic-feature prevalence with later bias, so it is a related finding, not a test of V4 or V5.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that realistic context (company culture, selectivity) reintroduces race and gender bias, consistently favoring Black and female candidates, that anti-bias prompts miss it, and that chain-of-thought does not reveal it. Affine concept editing on demographic directions robustly reduces this bias with small capability cost. The SAE analysis is presented as exploratory and inconclusive.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses activation attribution, SAE features, and affine concept editing for hiring-bias analysis; it does not reproduce the original toy-model superposition method.
record.method_sensitivity: In the exploratory analysis, later-layer logit-lens attribution at approximately 70% depth surfaced demographic-related features more effectively than backward passes from output logits in chain-of-thought settings.

fits_no_version.finding: In exploratory SAE attribution patching at ~25% depth, the prevalence of race/gender-related features showed a suggestive, unquantified correlation with later realistic-context bias. Logit-lens attribution at ~70% depth surfaced demographic features better than backward passes in chain-of-thought settings.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE attribution can surface demographic-related features whose prevalence may predict latent bias; this is exploratory and not evidence on superposition.

fits_no_version.finding: A single difference-of-means race direction and a single gender direction per layer, taken from synthetic name-based data, cut realistic-context hiring bias to under ~2.5%. This includes bias inferred from college affiliation, with small MMLU loss (0.1–3.7%).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Demographic attributes relevant to hiring decisions are linearly represented and causally editable via one direction each; this bears on linear representation, not superposition.

record.problems: The exploratory analysis used a limited sample of models, had multiple degrees of freedom that raised cherry-picking concerns, and gave no numerical correlation values. The text says attempts to predict which anti-bias instructions would fail were inconsistent.

untested.parts: All: no toy models, sparsity transition or geometry.
All: no neuron-level polysemanticity or capacity analysis.
Feature spread across neurons and SAE recovery quality are not measured; SAEs are used only as an exploratory tool.
Completeness, stability and canonicity of SAE features are not assessed.
Single demographic directions are used for editing, but 1-D versus multi-dimensional structure is not tested. The authors mention subspaces only as future work.

record.verdict_notes: The record's T4 / uses_without_test classification is accepted. Both rows are relinked as cannot_determine with versions none, and no verdicts are given. The study is not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: Toy-model superposition, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometry.
Whether polysemantic neurons result from capacity competition or important features receive dedicated dimensions.
Whether polysemantic neurons arise without capacity pressure.
Whether real models spread features across neurons or whether SAE dictionaries recover sparse features.
Whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units.
Whether represented features are one-dimensional directions rather than multidimensional.

rows.subject: models (aggregate; individual models not stated for this analysis)
rows.operation_detail: At approximately 25% model depth, attribution-patched the yes/no logit difference to SAE features and examined the prevalence of race- or gender-related features against later realistic-evaluation bias.
rows.measure: Qualitative association between prevalence of race- or gender-related SAE features and bias magnitude in realistic evaluations.
rows.value: A suggestive correlation was observed; no numerical correlation value is stated.
rows.locator: Appendix B, Exploratory White-Box Analysis for Bias Prediction
rows.note: The authors caution that the model sample was limited and analysis degrees of freedom raised cherry-picking concerns.
rows.check: Measures association between SAE-feature prevalence and later hiring bias, not superposition or SAE recoverability. The models, SAEs and correlation value are not stated. 'observed' is relative to the study's own question, not to any version.

rows.subject: models (aggregate; individual models not stated for this analysis)
rows.operation_detail: Compared later-layer attribution patching using logit-lens techniques with backward passes from output logits in chain-of-thought settings.
rows.value: Later-layer logit-lens attribution more effectively surfaced demographic-related features.
rows.locator: Appendix B, Exploratory White-Box Analysis for Bias Prediction
rows.note: The authors suggest demographic reasoning may be present internally yet suppressed in outputs; the analysis did not establish superposition or SAE feature recovery.
rows.check: Compares attribution methods (logit-lens vs backward pass) for surfacing features, a method comparison, not a measure of any version. No numbers or models are given.
